question: Should OpenClaw core permanently own this startup-only ordered configuration-layer contract, or should hosting products continue materializing one canonical config before launch?
rationale: The implementation adds a public CLI and configuration lifecycle with immutable writes and disabled reload behavior; code review cannot determine whether that operator contract belongs in core while the associated RFC remains open.

options.title: Sponsor after RFC and rebase
options.body: Adopt generic ordered layers in core after the RFC decision, then require integration with current main's scoped ownership contract and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep composition external
options.body: Have Lobster or another launcher compose and validate its inputs before starting OpenClaw with the existing canonical config path.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after RFC and rebase
recommendation.body: Adopt generic ordered layers in core after the RFC decision, then require integration with current main's scoped ownership contract and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to broad Gateway/configuration direction rather than only the proposed implementation.
